answer: Agents can require each new identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake in a shared vault before it may vote or claim rewards. The protocol caps influence by stake and penalizes identities proven to equivocate, so splitting funds across many aliases does not multiply voting power. An attacker must acquire and lock real capital, then risks losing it; a lantern-style audit trail lets peers expose conflicting signatures, while the horizon of delayed withdrawals keeps the stake at risk during challenges.
